extracted.subtask_description: Practical, prescriptive recipes and preparation standards for meats, pork curing, sausages, and many kinds of fish; aimed at producing correctly cooked and preserved dishes in a household kitchen.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fried lamb — portioning and presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Separate the leg from the loin, cut off the shank and boil the leg; divide the loin in chops, dredge and fry them a nice brown, lay the leg in the middle of the dish, and put the chops around, pour over parsley and butter, and garnish with fried parsley.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also: leg cut into steaks and the loin into chops will make a fine fricassee or cutlets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dressing lamb's head and feet — cleaning, stewing, and garnish
rubrics_metrics.description: Clean head and feet, boil till tender, take off flesh from head with the eyes, mince tongue and heart (boiled with head), split feet, stew pieces with minced meat in gravy seasoned with pepper, salt, and tomato catsup or ripe tomatoes, thicken gravy, lay liver broiled over it and garnish with crisp parsley and bits of curled bacon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use careful cleaning; mince and combine organ meats; include toasted bacon and crisp parsley for garnish.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mutton — roasting preference and seasonality
rubrics_metrics.description: The saddle should always be roasted and garnished with scraped horseradish. Mutton is in highest perfection from August until Christmas, when it begins to decline in goodness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow general observations on roasting; prefer roasting for the saddle; time of year affects quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boiled leg of mutton — preparation and finishing by steam
rubrics_metrics.description: Cut off the shank, wrap the flank and secure with skewers, dredge with flour, put in cold water with salt and 3–4 heads of garlic, skin it well; when nearly done keep hot and closely covered so steam finishes it; serve with boiled carrots or mashed turnips, and pour over melted butter with flour and a cup of capers mixed with some vinegar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use garlic for delicate flavour; let steam finish cooking to retain juices; melt butter with flour to make sauce and heat capers with vinegar before adding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Roasted leg of mutton — preparation and serving
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare as for boiling, be careful in spitting it, cover with paper, follow roasting directions, and serve garnished with scraped horseradish.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat preparation similarly to boiling but apply roasting technique; cover with paper to control browning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Baked leg of mutton — boning, stuffing, and flavoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Take the flank off but leave fat, cut out the bone, stuff with rich forcemeat, lard top and sides with bacon, bake in a pan with water, chopped onion and celery, a gill of red wine, mushroom catsup and a teaspoon of curry powder; bake and serve with the gravy and garnish with fried forcemeat balls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retain fat for flavour; use forcemeat and larding for richness; include mushroom catsup and curry for seasoning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Steaks from leg of mutton — cutting and serving
rubrics_metrics.description: Cut off the flank, remove bone, slice in large pieces ~½ inch thick, sprinkle salt and pepper, broil, pour melted butter with capers over them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leg cut similarly dressed like veal cutlets is also fine; can salt and boil like beef and serve with carrots or turnips.

rubrics_metrics.name: Harrico mutton — chops, gravy, and stewing
rubrics_metrics.description: Divide nicest part of rack into chops with bone, beat flat, salt and pepper, broil; make rich gravy from inferior parts seasoned with pepper, spice and catsup, thicken with butter and brown flour; add diced carrots and turnips boiled tender, stew chops 15 minutes in gravy and serve garnished with green pickle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use inferior parts to make rich gravy; include diced root vegetables; finish by stewing briefly to combine flavours.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mutton chops — broiling and light gravy
rubrics_metrics.description: Cut rack as for harrico, broil; pour over a gravy made with boiling water, mushroom catsup, a small spoonful of butter and salt; stir until butter melts and garnish with scraped horseradish.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simple pan gravy of water, catsup and butter suffices for chops.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boiled breast of mutton — jointing and service
rubrics_metrics.description: Separate brisket joints, saw off sharp rib ends, dredge with flour, and boil; serve covered with onions (see onion sauce).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preparation emphasises jointing and flour dredging; pair with onion sauce.

rubrics_metrics.name: Breast of mutton in ragout — browning and finishing
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare breast as for boiling, brown nicely in oven, use a rich gravy well seasoned and thickened with brown flour, stew until done and garnish with fried forcemeat balls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Browning first adds colour and flavour; use thickened gravy and forcemeat garnish.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grilled breast of mutton — breadcrumb crust
rubrics_metrics.description: Score top, wash with yolk of egg, sprinkle salt, cover with bread crumbs, bake, and pour caper sauce in the dish. Could also roast with skin taken off and frothed, served with good gravy and currant jelly slices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Egg wash and breadcrumbs create crust; provide caper sauce or gravy and sweet jelly as accompaniments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boiled shoulder of mutton — simple boiling and service
rubrics_metrics.description: Put in cold water with salt and boil till tender; serve covered with onion sauce.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Straightforward boiling; pair with onion sauce.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shoulder of mutton with celery sauce — sauce preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: Clean ten heads of celery, slice thin, boil tender in a little milk sufficient for gravy, add salt, thicken with butter and white flour; pour over boiled shoulder.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use milk to cook celery into a sauce; thicken and season to preference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Roasted loin of mutton — breadcrumb-parsley crust and packaging
rubrics_metrics.description: Cut loin into four pieces, remove skin, rub with salt, wash with yolk of egg, cover with bread crumbs, chopped parsley, pepper and salt; wrap securely in paper, put on a bird spit, roast; serve with a little brown gravy and garnish with pickle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Egg and breadcrumb-parsley crust and wrapping in paper preserve moisture and create crust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curing bacon — hog selection, salting, and smoking schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: Best hogs 2½–4 years old, not too heavy, fed with corn 6 weeks before killing, drive short distances; salt before cold; remove chine and cut hams, shoulders and middlings; rub saltpetre on hams briefly, rub both sides with salt, layer in tubs with salt between layers; salt shoulders and middlings with less saltpetre; salt jowl/chop; hang jowls after 2 weeks to smoke, shoulders/middlings after 3 weeks, hams after 4 weeks; do not leave too long in salt or juices are drawn off; hang hams and shoulders with hocks down to preserve juices; maintain steady smoke daily, avoid blaze; smoke-house should stand alone; during hot weather occasionally take down and rub with hickory ashes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Saltpetre prevents putrefaction but does not harden meat; too long in salt hardens; boil bacon in large quantity water; a ham is done when bone comes off under part with ease.

rubrics_metrics.name: Making souse — soaking, cleaning, boiling and preserving
rubrics_metrics.description: Soak pieces in cold water 12 hours, wash repeatedly, scrape and clean, mix meal with water and salt and boil souse gently until a straw will enter skin easily; cook feet, ears, nose, heads separately; season insides with pepper, salt and nutmeg; roll in cloth and press lightly; mix more meal and cold water with 1/4 vinegar, pour over cooled souse in pots and stop closely; renew liquor every 2–3 weeks; use pale-coloured vinegar to keep souse white; do not singe hair as it destroys colour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frequent water changes draw out blood; small pots and careful boiling preserve appearance; keep souse cool before adding preserving liquor; renew cover liquor periodically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Roasting a pig — stuffing, basting, and carving
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose a very fat pig, clean and not too large; make stuffing from liver, bread crumbs, onion, parsley, pepper, salt, butter and egg; stuff body firmly, sew up and spit roast over clear fire; baste initially with salt and water, then frequently with lard wrapped in clean linen for crispness; when done, remove head, split pig, serve with stuffing mixed with wine and dripping.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use lard-basting for crisp skin; careful carving and presentation include head, ears and feet placed decoratively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Barbecue shote (young hog) — quartering, stuffing and baking
rubrics_metrics.description: Cut shote into quarters, make incisions and stuff with rich forcemeat, bake in pan with water, garlic, pepper, salt, red wine and mushroom catsup, thicken gravy with batter and brown flour; joint and cut ribs across for carving; lay ribs uppermost and garnish with balls; if not brown enough add burnt sugar to gravy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure jointing and rib cuts for easy carving; use burnt sugar sparingly to enhance browning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Roasting a fore-quarter of shote — jointing, roasting, and service
rubrics_metrics.description: Joint for carving, roast before brisk fire; when done remove skin, dredge and froth, serve with melted butter and caper vinegar or mint sauce.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Jointing improves carving; frothing the skin enhances appearance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shote cutlets — using hind-quarter skin and scraps for gravy
rubrics_metrics.description: Remove skin from hind-quarter, cut into pieces and prepare as veal cutlets; make gravy from skin and scraps, thicken with butter and brown flour and season to taste.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use scraps and skin to make a flavorful gravy to accompany cutlets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corn shote (salt-cured) — rub with saltpetre and salt
rubrics_metrics.description: Rub hind-quarter with saltpetre and common salt, let lie ten days, then boil and serve with carrots or parsnips under it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simple dry curing with saltpetre and salt for quick curing before boiling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shote's head — boiling, mincing, and composed presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Boil head till tender, remove brains, mince tongue and chop brains small, boil feet with head, mince meat, season with onion, parsley, thyme, catsup, thicken with butter and brown flour, stew 15 minutes, serve with roasted heart in middle, broiled liver around and garnish with green pickle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assemble organ meats thoughtfully; use thickened gravy and decorative arrangement for presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leg of pork with pease pudding — salting, boiling and pudding handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Boil a small sufficiently salted leg, score top and serve; pease pudding made separately from small delicate peas, washed and tied in a cloth with room for swelling, boiled with pork, then mashed, seasoned and tied again to finish; take care not to break pudding when turning out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare pudding separately to avoid breaking; tie to allow swelling; match salt levels to the pork.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stewed chine — salting and baking with sweet potatoes
rubrics_metrics.description: Rub neck chine well with salt, lay in pan with a pint of water and sweet potatoes (washed but not peeled), cover close and bake till done; serve with potatoes and some gravy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use unpeeled sweet potatoes and bake tightly covered to stew in own juices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Toasting a ham — boiling then browning crust
rubrics_metrics.description: Boil ham well, remove skin, cover thickly with bread crumbs, brown in oven and serve.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure ham is well boiled before applying breadcrumb crust for toasting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stuffing a ham — making incisions and cold serving
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a well smoked ham, wash, make incisions ~2 inches deep, stuff with finely chopped parsley and pepper, boil sufficiently but do not remove skin; must be eaten cold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep skin to contain stuffing; serve cold for best texture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Soused feet in ragout — splitting, frying and stewing briefly
rubrics_metrics.description: Split feet in two, dredge with flour and fry light brown; prepare seasoned gravy thickened with brown flour and butter, stew feet a few minutes and serve.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frying gives colour before quick stewing in ragout to finish.

rubrics_metrics.name: Making sausages — meat-to-fat ratio and seasoning
rubrics_metrics.description: Chop tender fresh pork very fine and leaf fat; proportion three pounds pork to one pound fat, season highly with pepper and salt, add small quantity dried sage rubbed to powder, prepare skins and fill, hang in a dry place. Sausages may be fried in cakes but will not keep as well.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain 3:1 meat-to-fat ratio; high seasoning and proper casing preparation are essential for texture and preservation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Making black puddings — blood handling and binding
rubrics_metrics.description: Catch blood as it runs and stir until cold to prevent coagulation; thicken with boiled rice or oatmeal, add leaf fat chopped, pepper, salt and herbs, fill skins and smoke 2–3 days; boil before hanging and prick with fork to prevent bursting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continuous stirring prevents premature coagulation; binders like rice/oatmeal and smoking improve stability; boil first to set.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sea pie — layering and moist baking
rubrics_metrics.description: Layer boiled pork or salt beef slices, potatoes, onions, herbs, soaked crackers, and fowls or veal in small Dutch oven; put butter between layers, pour water/wine/catsup and pounded cloves until it reaches top crust, stew until just gravy remains; serve in a deep dish and pour remaining gravy on.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use butter between layers and sufficient liquid; cook until concentrated gravy remains for richness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Savory paste for pies — hot fat method
rubrics_metrics.description: Pour ½ lb butter or dripping boiling hot into a quart of flour, add water to make a paste, work and roll well.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hot fat technique creates a savoury, workable paste.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bologna sausages — proportions and boiling
rubrics_metrics.description: Use equal portions of bacon, veal, pork and suet (one pound each), chop fine, season highly, fill skins, prick and boil one hour, hang to dry; grated bread or boiled rice may be added.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Par-boiling then drying preserves sausages; addition of bread or rice alters texture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curing herrings — using brine and barrel salting
rubrics_metrics.description: Use brine from winter beef stock, pick large herrings and throw alive into brine for 24 hours, drain on sloping planks; in tight barrel put coarse alum salt at bottom, layer herrings with alum salt and saltpetre, add brine if needed to keep under brine; fat herrings are best (scales loose), do not be sparing of salt; when used soak, scale, remove gills, wash and dry; for broiling wrap in buttered paper and broil without burning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pick fat herrings at season; keep under brine to avoid rustiness; generous salting for preservation; use brine for flavour retention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Baking sturgeon — cleaning, pre-boil oil removal, stuffing and sauce
rubrics_metrics.description: Select piece next to tail with skin on, scrape and remove gristle, boil ~20 minutes to take out oil, pull off large scales when cold, stuff with forcemeat of crumbs, butter, parsley, pepper and salt, put in Dutch oven with water, red wine, mushroom catsup, salt and pepper, stew till gravy reduces; thicken gravy with butter rubbed into brown flour; ensure gravy is perfectly smooth when serving.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-boil to remove oiliness; preserve skin for appearance; reduce gravy and strain for smoothness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sturgeon cutlets and steaks — slicing, frying and saucing
rubrics_metrics.description: Use tail piece, skin and remove gristle, slice ~½ inch, season, dredge with flour, fry light brown; prepare pint of gravy seasoned with catsup, wine and pounded cloves, thickened with brown flour and butter; for cutlets put cold cutlets in gravy to stew a few minutes; steaks served quickly with melted butter and chopped parsley.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tail piece preferred; finish cutlets by briefly stewing in sauce for flavour absorption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boiling sturgeon — skin, salting and rich sauce
rubrics_metrics.description: Leave skin on (scraped), remove gristle, rub with salt and let lie an hour, put in cold water with salt and garlic, dredge with flour before putting in, skim carefully; when dished pour melted butter with parsley, mushroom catsup, lemon pickle and pepper vinegar; send sauce boat for additional mixing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain skin for presentation; salt in advance to season; rich sauce needed as sturgeon is a dry fish.

rubrics_metrics.name: Baking a shad — forcemeat, stewing and careful dishing
rubrics_metrics.description: Use large fat shad, prepare with forcemeat inside, lay in pan with water, red wine, mushroom catsup, pepper, vinegar, salt, garlic and cloves; stew gently till gravy reduces; use fish-slice with holes for dishing to avoid breakage; thicken gravy with butter and brown flour and pour over fish.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select large fat specimens; use holey fish-slice to preserve whole fish when transferring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boiling a shad — fresh fish and sauce accompaniment
rubrics_metrics.description: Use fresh fat shad to prevent skin cracking, boil in cold water on a slice with pale vinegar, salt, garlic and parsley bundle; when done drain water, garnish with scraped horseradish and provide melted butter mixed with catsups in sauce boat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Freshness prevents skin damage; offer sauce boat for individual preference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Roasting and broiling shad — stuffing, bread crumb crust and careful turning
rubrics_metrics.description: For roasting fill cavity with forcemeat, sew and tie on board, cover with breadcrumbs and roast turning as necessary; for broiling separate one side from backbone to lie flat, dry, salt/pepper and broil on hot greased gridiron, pour melted butter when served.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tying on a board maintains shape; proper preparation prevents splitting during cooking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boiling rock fish — using head and shoulders and serving with sauces
rubrics_metrics.description: Best part is head and shoulders; clean, boil gently and skim well; serve with scraped horseradish and two sauce boats of tatter melted with parsley or anchovy butter; fry roe and liver in separate dishes; leftover rock makes fine next-day dish when stewed with butter, lemon pickle and pepper vinegar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Head and shoulders prized; provide two sauce options; repurpose leftovers into a quick stew.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frying perch — drying, flouring and hot lard
rubrics_metrics.description: Clean but do not take out roes, dry on cloth, salt and dredge with flour on both sides, ensure lard is boiling when fish is put in and fry carefully until yellowish brown; serve with melted butter or anchovy sauce.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not remove roes for certain presentations; temperature control of fat is essential for proper browning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pickling oysters — selecting large oysters and vinegar liquor
rubrics_metrics.description: Select largest oysters, drain liquor and wash, remove shell pieces, stew briefly in water with salt, blades of mace and whole pepper; when cold add pale vinegar to give agreeable acid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use pale vinegar for colour and agreeable acidity; do not overcook oysters in stewing step.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curry of catfish — stewing down and gravy finishing
rubrics_metrics.description: Take white channel catfish, clean and cut into ~4 inch pieces, stew with water, two onions and parsley until reduced to half pint, remove fish, rub butter into flour, add curry powder, thicken gravy and pour over fish ensuring gravy is smooth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reduce stock to concentrate flavour; ensure smoothness of thickened curry gravy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dressing a cod's head and shoulders — boiling, scraping and frothing
rubrics_metrics.description: Remove gills and blood, rub a little salt, boil ½–¾ hour depending on size (¾ for large), strip skin, set before brisk fire, dredge with flour and baste well with butter until froth rises, throw fine white bread crumbs over when frothing to brown, garnish with lemon, horseradish, barberries and small fried fish or oysters; include lobster out of sauce in lumps if desired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frothing with butter and bread crumbs creates a brown crust; careful dishing to maintain shape and garnishes elevates presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sauce for cod's head (lobster-based) — using lobster spawn and butter
rubrics_metrics.description: Boil live lobster, pound spawn fine in mortar and add to ½ lb melted butter, add meat pulled in bits, lemon pickle, walnut catsup, lemon slice, horse-radish, beaten mace, salt and cayenne; boil one minute, remove lemon and horse-radish and serve.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no lobster available, substitute shrimp, cockle or mussel sauce or anchovies and walnut liquor with an onion stuck with cloves and strain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dressing salt cod — steeping, boiling and serving
rubrics_metrics.description: Steep salt cod in water all night with a glass of vinegar to take out salt, then boil, remove skin, pull in flakes, and serve with egg sauce or mashed parsnips with butter and cream; serve on water plate as it cools quickly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Steeping with vinegar reduces saltiness; serve promptly on water plate to avoid cooling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matelote for firm fish — pieces, aromatics, wine reduction, and thickening
rubrics_metrics.description: Cut fish into 6-inch pieces, cook with onion, parsley, thyme, mushrooms, spice, pepper and salt, add red wine and water, reduce by one-third and thicken with butter and flour, serve with bits of fried bread in dish.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use wine reduction and aromatics to enrich firm fish; fry bread bits for texture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chowder (sea dish) — layering, crackers and wine
rubrics_metrics.description: Use firm fish cut in 6-inch pieces, sprinkle salt and pepper, layer in small Dutch oven over partially boiled salt pork and chopped onion, cover with soaked crackers, pour two gills white wine and two gills water, stew ~1 hour, thicken gravy with flour and butter, add chopped parsley and serve hot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Soaked crackers act as binder and thickener; include wine for flavour; cook gently to meld flavours.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pickling sturgeon — preserving skin and rolling
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose small sturgeon ~4 feet, keep skin on, cut off gristle, scrape skin, wash and salt 24 hours, wipe salt off, roll and tie with twine, boil until straw enters skin easily, pull off large scales, when cold put in pot with 1 part vinegar to 2 parts salt and water, keep stopped and garnish with green fennel when served.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep skin for appearance; rolling and tying aids storage; brine proportion specified for preservation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caveach fish — frying and oil-vinegar marinade
rubrics_metrics.description: Cut fish into hand-thick pieces, wash and dry, season with pepper and salt, dredge with flour and fry brown; when cold layer with chopped onion, cover with vinegar and water mixed with oil, pounded mace and whole black pepper and stop closely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use as a ready addition to meals; garnish with fennel or parsley when served.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dressing cod fish (en croûte baking) — mixing fish with vegetables and baking
rubrics_metrics.description: Boil fish tender, pick from bones, take equal quantity of potatoes or parsnips boiled and chopped and onions, add melted butter, grated nutmeg, pepper, salt and a little brandy or wine, rub in mortar until mixed, if too stiff liquify with cream or milk, line dish with paste and bake (or form into patties).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use equal vegetable filler to fish; add spirit for flavour; binder/moistening with cream as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cod fish pie — fish-to-bread ratio and richness
rubrics_metrics.description: Soak and boil fish, remove skin, mince very fine; use double quantity stale bread grated to fish, wet with boiling milk, add minced parsley, nutmeg, pepper, made mustard and melted butter to make rich mixture; fill pastry and bake with lid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High proportion of grated bread creates texture and bulk; boiling milk used to hydrate crumb binder.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dressing any kind of salted fish — soaking and aromatic simmer
rubrics_metrics.description: Soak necessary quantity overnight, place on tin plate with holes in fish kettle, sprinkle pounded cloves and pepper, add garlic, sweet herbs, parsley, tarragon and vinegar with a pint of wine; roll ¼ lb butter into two spoonsful of flour, cut into small pieces and put over fish, cover and simmer ½ hour; strain out garlic and herbs, pour over fish and serve (good cold with salad).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concentrated aromatics and butter-flour pieces enrich salted fish; can be served cold as salad accompaniment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fricasseeing cod sounds and tongues — soaking, boiling and allemande-style sauce
rubrics_metrics.description: Soak overnight, remove skins, cut in two and boil in milk and water until tender, drain, season with nutmeg, pepper and little salt; make sauce with new milk and butter-rolled-in-flour and stir fish in until thick enough.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Milk-based poaching and sauce preserves delicate texture; season lightly.

rubrics_metrics.name: An excellent way to dress fish (reheated in sauce) — dredging, frying and saucing
rubrics_metrics.description: Dredge fish with flour, sprinkle salt and pepper, fry to light brown and set aside cold; fry tomatoes (peels off), parsley and a little chopped onion in butter, add water with pepper, salt and pounded cloves, add wine and mushroom catsup, put fish in and reheat in sauce until thoroughly heated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technique is to fry first, then reheat in a smooth sauce for a different flavour profile; ensure sauce smoothness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fish a-la-daub and fish in jelly — poaching, setting and presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Boil whole white perch without removing heads or breaking skins; when cold place in dish and cover with savoury jelly (made from hog's feet, light coloured and transparent) or use blanc mange-filled moulds set in jelly for decorative effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep fish whole and intact; transparent jelly for elegant presentation; use molds to create decorative elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Egg sauce for salt cod — chopping and mixing with butter
rubrics_metrics.description: Boil four eggs hard, chop whites and yelks together (not very small), mix into ½ lb good melted butter, let boil up and pour on fish.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coarse chop preserves texture; pour boiling egg-butter mixture to warm and season fish.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dressing cod sounds — soaking and milk boiling with egg sauce
rubrics_metrics.description: Steep sounds as for salt cod, boil in large quantity milk and water until very tender and white, drain and skin, pour hot egg sauce over and serve.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use substantial milk poaching to whiten sounds; pair with boiling-hot egg-butter sauce.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stewing carp — dredging, frying then stewing in wine-based gravy
rubrics_metrics.description: Gut, scale, dredge and fry until light brown, then stew in pan with ½ pint red wine, ½ pint water, lemon pickle, walnut catsup, mushroom powder, cayenne, onion stuck with cloves and horse-radish; cover and reduce gravy to just enough to cover fish, then thicken with flour and butter and garnish with pickled mushrooms and horseradish.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine initial frying for colour with richly seasoned wine-based stew; adjust gravy reduction to cover.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boiling eels — simple boiling with parsley sauce
rubrics_metrics.description: Clean and cut off heads, dry and coil on fish plate, boil in salt water and serve with parsley sauce.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep presentation coiled; pair with classic parsley sauce.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pitchcock eels — skewering and broiling
rubrics_metrics.description: Skin, wash and dry eels, season with pepper, salt and dried sage, skewer, rub gridiron with beef suet, broil to nice brown and serve with melted butter and fried parsley.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Skewering aids even cooking; beef suet lubricates gridiron for flavour and release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broiling eels with breadcrumb crust — egg wash and crumbs
rubrics_metrics.description: Skin and cleanse, rub with yolk of egg, strew bread crumbs, chopped parsley, sage, pepper and salt, baste with butter and set in dripping pan; serve with parsley and butter sauce.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Egg wash and breadcrumbs form a crust suitable for broiling; baste well for moisture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scollop oysters — layering and browning in shells
rubrics_metrics.description: Wash oysters out of liquor, put in scallop shells, strew bread crumbs and a slice of butter alternately and brown in Dutch oven, serve in shells.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use own liquor and buttered crumbs to create gratin-style scallops.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frying oysters — breading and frying to light brown
rubrics_metrics.description: Wash oysters, roll in grated bread with pepper and salt, fry to light brown; may add parsley; proper garnish for calves' head or made dishes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seasoned breading and controlled frying produce proper colour; use as garnish or main.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oyster loaves — filling hollowed loaves with creamy oyster stew and crisping
rubrics_metrics.description: Hollow small round loaves, stew oysters with crumbs from loaves in a little water and butter 10–15 minutes, add spoonful of cream, fill loaves, replace top and crisp in oven.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use loaf crumbs in stew for body and replace lid for neat presentation and crisp finish.
